articles.title: She Walked Back From Injury. She Walked England Into a World Cup Final. Nat Sciver-Brunt's 75 Was the Innings of the Tournament.
articles.excerpt: England captain returns from a calf strain, rescues her side from 23 for 3, and fires them into a Lord's final against Australia with a 133-run stand alongside Heather Knight.
articles.image_caption: Nat Sciver-Brunt batting for England in international cricket
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in the UK have had front-row seats to a record-breaking Women's T20 World Cup, with the Lord's final and a historic women's Test against India both days away.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ashwin and Dravid Reunite in Dublin. Europe's First ICC-Sanctioned T20 League Just Got Its Star Power.
articles.excerpt: The European T20 Premier League held its inaugural draft on Thursday, with Ashwin captaining Dravid's franchise and Maxwell, Steve Waugh and Jonty Rhodes all owning teams across Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands.
articles.image_caption: Ravichandran Ashwin during an international match for India
articles.nri_angle: The ETPL brings franchise cricket to Dublin, Belfast, Edinburgh and Glasgow — cities with large Indian and South Asian diaspora populations — letting NRIs in the UK and Europe watch Ashwin and Maxwell play on their doorstep.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Will Play Their First Test Series in Sri Lanka Since 2017. Here's What's at Stake.
articles.excerpt: Two World Test Championship matches at Galle and Colombo in August mark India's return to the island after an eight-year gap — with their WTC final hopes hanging in the balance.
articles.image_caption: Shubman Gill, India's Test captain, will lead the side in Sri Lanka
articles.nri_angle: Galle is one of the easiest and most popular overseas cricket destinations for Indian fans, and the first Test falls on India's Independence Day — making it a potential travel pilgrimage for NRIs across Asia and the Middle East.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'She's Stagnated.' Diana Edulji Wants Harmanpreet Kaur and Amol Muzumdar Gone After India's T20 World Cup Exit.
articles.excerpt: India's first women's ODI captain says fresh leadership and a new coaching mind are overdue — but the BCCI has already backed Harmanpreet for the Asian Games.
articles.image_caption: India women's cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur during a T20 international
articles.nri_angle: India's ODI World Cup triumph last year was a landmark for diaspora fans — this T20 failure and the leadership debate that follows will shape the next chapter of a team NRIs have invested enormous pride in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Virat Kohli Has Not Played a Single MLC Match — and Mi New York’s Bench Might Be the Most Star-Studded in Cricket History
articles.excerpt: The defending champions’ registered squad includes Kohli, AB de Villiers, Chris Gayle, Kane Williamson, Joe Root, and Glenn Phillips — none of whom have been in the playing XI as the season enters its third week.
articles.image_caption: Virat Kohli at the Prime Minister’s Office in New Delhi after India’s T20 World Cup victory in July 2024.

articles.title: Gardner and Perry Won't Be Stopped. Australia Crush West Indies to Reach Another Women's T20 World Cup Final.
articles.excerpt: An eight-wicket demolition at The Oval sends Australia into Sunday's final at Lord's — the same ground where they ended India's campaign four days ago. England or South Africa will be their opponent.
articles.image_caption: Ellyse Perry, whose half-century against India and consistent performances have powered Australia's run to the Women's T20 World Cup final
articles.nri_angle: India's second consecutive group-stage exit puts pressure on the Harmanpreet Kaur era, while NRIs in the UK can attend the final at Lord's — but will be watching as neutrals after their team's heartbreak at the same venue.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Conceded a Point He'd Won. Then He Lost the Final He'd Earned. Kidambi Srikanth's Nine-Year Wait Goes On.
articles.excerpt: The former world No. 1 reached the US Open badminton final in Fullerton, California, at 33 — and left with his fourth runner-up finish and one of the year's great acts of sportsmanship.
articles.image_caption: Kidambi Srikanth in action during a BWF tournament
articles.nri_angle: The US Open was held in Fullerton, California — deep in Orange County's Indian-American heartland — giving NRI badminton fans a rare chance to watch a former world No. 1 compete on home turf.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Balogun Scored. Then He Was Sent Off. Ten-Man USA Beat Bosnia 2-0 in the Bay Area to Reach the World Cup Round of 16.
articles.excerpt: Folarin Balogun’s third goal of the tournament and a stunning Malik Tillman free kick powered the Americans past Bosnia at Levi’s Stadium — ending a 24-year wait for a knockout-stage win, with NRIs in Silicon Valley celebrating alongside them.
articles.image_caption: Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, the Bay Area venue that hosted the USA vs Bosnia World Cup match
articles.nri_angle: The World Cup Round of 32 match was played at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara — the heart of Silicon Valley — making it a once-in-a-generation live sporting event for Bay Area NRIs, many of whom have adopted American soccer as a second sporting passion.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tielemans in the 125th Minute. Belgium Came Back From the Dead in Seattle — and NRIs in the Pacific Northwest Had Front-Row Seats.
articles.excerpt: Down 2-0 with four minutes left, Belgium staged the World Cup's most dramatic comeback yet. Youri Tielemans scored twice, including a 125th-minute penalty after a controversial VAR call, to sink Senegal 3-2 in extra time at Lumen Field.
articles.image_caption: Youri Tielemans in Belgium colors during the March 2026 friendly against the United States
articles.nri_angle: Seattle's 100,000+ Indian tech community had front-row seats to the World Cup's most dramatic comeback — and Belgium's Round of 16 match is also at Lumen Field, keeping the tournament in the Pacific Northwest NRI heartland.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kane Scores Twice, Passes Pelé. England Survive DR Congo and Head to the Azteca.
articles.excerpt: Harry Kane's 75th and 86th minute goals rescued England from the brink of elimination in Atlanta, pushing him past Pelé's all-time World Cup record. Next up: co-hosts Mexico in one of football's most hostile arenas.
articles.image_caption: Harry Kane in action for England — the Bayern Munich striker now has 13 World Cup goals
articles.nri_angle: With the World Cup on American soil, millions of NRIs are watching history unfold in their own cities — from Kane's record-breaking night in Atlanta to tonight's USA match in the Bay Area.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Unbeaten and Unbowed. India Women Win the Nations Cup and Earn Their Way Back to the Pro League.
articles.excerpt: Five wins from five. A 2-0 final victory over hosts New Zealand in Auckland. And the prize that matters most: promotion back to the FIH Pro League after last season's relegation.
articles.image_caption: India women in action during an international hockey match
articles.nri_angle: India women's hockey team's Nations Cup triumph and Pro League return fuel hopes for the LA 2028 Olympics, where hockey remains one of India's strongest medal prospects.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Abhishek Sharma Blazed 59 off 24 Balls. Shreyas Iyer Made 68. Rain Made It All Count for Nothing.
articles.excerpt: India posted 189/7 after being reduced to 6/2, but persistent rain in Durham washed out England's chase and the series opener ended without a result
articles.image_caption: Abhishek Sharma in action during an international match
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of NRI fans across the UK who packed the Riverside Ground for the series opener were denied a full contest as rain washed out India's strong performance
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The IPL's Biggest Boardroom Battle Is Here. Franchise Owners Are Split on How Many Players to Keep.
articles.excerpt: The BCCI will meet IPL franchise owners at the end of July to finalize retention rules for the mega auction — with the salary cap set to rise to ₹120 crore and a fierce debate over whether the mega auction should even exist.
articles.image_caption: The Wankhede Stadium complex in Mumbai, home to BCCI headquarters where franchise owners will meet to decide IPL retention rules
articles.nri_angle: The mega auction is appointment viewing for NRIs worldwide — retention rules will determine whether Kohli stays at RCB, Rohit stays at MI, and whether Pandya enters the open market.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Seven Franchises Want Him. Hardik Pandya's Mumbai Indians Chapter Is Heading for Its Final Page.
articles.excerpt: Only RCB and SRH are sitting this one out. From CSK to KKR to Rajasthan Royals, the most contested IPL trade in years is shaping up — and the off-season drama is just getting started.
articles.image_caption: Hardik Pandya during an IPL match for Mumbai Indians
articles.nri_angle: The IPL trade window has become appointment viewing for NRI fans worldwide — Pandya's move will reshape the league that connects the diaspora to Indian cricket year-round.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The World Cup Bracket Is Set — and It’s Coming to Your Neighborhood
articles.excerpt: From Mbappé vs Paraguay in Philadelphia to Haaland vs Brazil at MetLife, the Round of 16 spans every major Indian-American hub and kicks off on the Fourth of July.
articles.image_caption: MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey — host of the World Cup Final on July 19 and the blockbuster Brazil vs Norway Round of 16 clash on July 5. (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Round of 16 venues — Houston, MetLife (NJ), Philadelphia, Seattle, Atlanta, Arlington, Vancouver — map almost perfectly onto the largest Indian-American population centers. For millions of NRIs, this is the first World Cup they can attend in person.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ishan Kishan Rises to World No.1 in T20I Rankings Ahead of England Series — Only the Fourth Indian to Reach the Summit
articles.excerpt: The wicketkeeper-batter overtakes teammate Abhishek Sharma in the latest ICC update, capping a remarkable comeback from a two-year exile
articles.image_caption: Ishan Kishan, India's new No.1 ranked T20I batter, has completed a remarkable rise from a mental health break to the top of the world rankings.
articles.nri_angle: Indian batter reaching world No.1 in T20I rankings ahead of a series on English soil is a point of pride for NRI cricket fans. Kishan's comeback from mental health challenges resonates with diaspora themes of resilience and reinvention.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ashwin in America. Cricket Has Never Had This Kind of Star Power on U.S. Soil.
articles.excerpt: India's greatest modern spinner made his MLC debut for the Bay Area's San Francisco Unicorns — and the league's third season is starting to look like the one that changes everything.
articles.image_caption: Ravichandran Ashwin in bowling action during a Test match at Trent Bridge in 2018
articles.nri_angle: The Bay Area's Indian diaspora finally has a cricket icon playing competitive matches in their backyard — Ashwin's MLC debut connects millions of NRIs to the sport on American soil.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Lightning, Hotel Serenades and Two Ruthless Goals. Mexico Own the Azteca — and the World Cup Round of 16 Awaits.
articles.excerpt: Quiñones and Jiménez score first-half stunners as co-hosts shut out Ecuador 2-0 at a raucous Estadio Azteca. The Round of 16 kicks off Saturday in Houston, Philadelphia and New Jersey — cities NRIs call home.
articles.image_caption: Estadio Azteca in Mexico City, dressed for the 2026 FIFA World Cup
articles.nri_angle: NRIs across North America are experiencing the World Cup in their own cities — Houston, New Jersey, the Bay Area — making the Round of 16 feel local for the first time.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iyer Says His 'Hands Are Tied.' India's Biggest Selection Dilemma Heads Into the England Series Unresolved.
articles.excerpt: The captain called it 'very private,' defended the World Cup winners, and refused to confirm whether Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will finally get his debut at Chester-le-Street on Wednesday.
articles.image_caption: India T20I captain Shreyas Iyer at a pre-match press conference
articles.nri_angle: NRI cricket fans in the UK are watching the Sooryavanshi debut saga unfold at English grounds they have historically filled — and many are desperate to see the teenage prodigy unleashed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mbappé Scores Twice. France Demolish Sweden 3-0 and He's Now One Goal From Messi's All-Time Record.
articles.excerpt: The French captain's double at MetLife Stadium lifts his World Cup tally to 18 — one behind Lionel Messi — as Les Bleus set up a Round of 16 clash with Paraguay in Philadelphia.
articles.image_caption: Kylian Mbappé during France's World Cup 2026 group stage match against Senegal
articles.nri_angle: The World Cup unfolding in NRI metro areas — MetLife in NJ, Levi's in Santa Clara — is creating shared sporting moments for Indian-Americans who straddle cricket and football cultures.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: She Came Back. She Lost. But Serena Williams at 44 on Centre Court Was the Moment Wimbledon Needed.
articles.excerpt: Four years after her last singles match, Williams accepted a wildcard, fought through a second-set tiebreak for the ages, and bowed out to 20-year-old Maya Joint 6-3, 6-7(6), 6-3 — then confirmed she'll play doubles with Venus on Thursday.
articles.image_caption: Serena Williams competing at Wimbledon
articles.nri_angle: Serena's comeback resonates with Indian fans who watched legends like Tendulkar and Dhoni return beyond their prime — and NRIs following Wimbledon amid India's singles drought adds emotional weight.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: No Pandya. No Nitish. India Walk Into England With an All-Rounder Void They Cannot Hide.
articles.excerpt: Nitish Kumar Reddy's quadriceps injury rules him out of the T20I series against England. With Hardik Pandya already in rehab, India are banking on a 23-year-old debutant to fill the gap.
articles.image_caption: Nitish Kumar Reddy during the Border-Gavaskar Trophy in 2024
articles.nri_angle: India's white-ball tour of England starts tomorrow, and NRI fans across the US and UK are watching a squad arrive without its two best all-rounders — a depth crisis that shapes the World Cup cycle.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Haaland’s Late Winner Sends Norway Past Ivory Coast and Into a World Cup Showdown With Brazil
articles.excerpt: The Manchester City striker scored his fifth goal of the tournament in the 86th minute, securing Norway’s first-ever knockout win at a World Cup — and setting up a rematch 28 years in the making.
articles.image_caption: Erling Haaland during Norway’s pre-World Cup friendly against Morocco in June 2026.
articles.image_credit: Bryan Berlin / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0
articles.nri_angle: World Cup on American soil brings the beautiful game to NRIs’ doorstep — from the DFW metroplex’s growing South Asian community to the 700,000-strong Indian-American population in the NY/NJ metro area. Norway’s next match at MetLife Stadium puts the tournament’s biggest storyline in the heart of the country’s largest NRI hub.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Haaland in the 86th Minute. Norway Break Ivory Coast Hearts in Arlington to Set Up a Date With Brazil.
articles.excerpt: Erling Haaland's fifth goal of the tournament and Antonio Nusa's curling strike send Norway into the Round of 16, where they will face Brazil in New Jersey on Sunday.
articles.image_caption: Erling Haaland in action during Norway's World Cup 2026 campaign
articles.nri_angle: The match was played in Arlington, TX — home to one of the largest Indian communities in the US — and Norway's next game is at MetLife Stadium in NJ, giving NRI fans front-row seats to the World Cup knockout rounds.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hardik Pandya Leaves Mumbai Behind. The BCCI Centre of Excellence Is Now His Permanent Home.
articles.excerpt: The 32-year-old all-rounder has moved to Bengaluru, hired his own physio and S&C coach, and is paying net bowlers from his own pocket — all to extend his career through the 2027 World Cup and the 2028 LA Olympics.
articles.image_caption: Hardik Pandya at the Prime Minister's Office in New Delhi
articles.nri_angle: Pandya's commitment to extending his career through the 2028 LA Olympics means NRIs in America could watch him play cricket at the Games on home soil — a first in 128 years.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Seven Goals. One Statement. India Demolish Pakistan in London to Send a Message Before the Hockey World Cup.
articles.excerpt: Harmanpreet Singh's side turned a 1-0 deficit into a 7-1 rout at Lee Valley, with seven different scorers reminding the hockey world and NRIs across the UK that this Indian team means business heading into August.
articles.image_caption: The Indian men's national field hockey team contingent
articles.nri_angle: Indian fans across the UK got a rare chance to watch their hockey team live at Lee Valley, and the 7-1 result sends a statement to NRIs ahead of the World Cup where India face Pakistan again in Pool D.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The World Cup Comes to Silicon Valley. For NRIs in the Bay Area, It's Already Home.
articles.excerpt: The USA face Bosnia and Herzegovina at Levi's Stadium on Wednesday — and for the half-million Indian Americans living within driving distance, football's biggest party is unfolding in their own backyard.
articles.image_caption: Aerial view of Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California, home to Wednesday's World Cup knockout match
articles.nri_angle: For half a million Indian Americans in Silicon Valley, the World Cup knockout match at Levi's Stadium is football's biggest party in their own backyard.

articles.title: Diop's Header. Bounou's Save. Morocco Stun the Netherlands in a Monterrey Shootout.
articles.excerpt: A 91st-minute equaliser and a penalty-shootout masterclass send Morocco past the Dutch and into a Round of 16 date with Canada in Houston — continuing the Atlas Lions' transformation into a genuine World Cup force.
articles.image_caption: Morocco goalkeeper Yassine Bounou during the 2026 FIFA World Cup
articles.nri_angle: The World Cup on North American soil continues to deliver drama for the Indian diaspora — Morocco's penalty heroics in Monterrey set the stage for the knockout rounds arriving in Houston, the Bay Area, and other NRI-heavy cities this week.

articles.title: Humbled in Belfast, India Arrive in England With Questions They Cannot Ignore
articles.excerpt: After a historic 0-2 whitewash by Ireland, Shreyas Iyer's India face a full-strength England in a five-match T20I series starting Wednesday. The biggest question: will Vaibhav Sooryavanshi finally play?
articles.image_caption: Shreyas Iyer, India's T20I captain, faces his biggest test in England after a humbling series loss to Ireland
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in the UK can watch India live across five English venues starting July 1 — and with India reeling from an Irish embarrassment, the diaspora will be watching closely to see if the world champions can regroup on familiar cricket soil.

articles.title: Germany Is Out. Paraguay's Goalkeeper Rewrote World Cup History in Boston.
articles.excerpt: Orlando Gill saved two penalties as Paraguay stunned the four-time champions 4-3 in a shootout — Germany's first-ever World Cup penalty loss. The tournament's biggest upset yet unfolded 30 miles from downtown Boston, in front of thousands of diaspora fans.
articles.image_caption: Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, where Paraguay eliminated Germany on penalty kicks
articles.nri_angle: The World Cup's biggest upset unfolded in Foxborough, Massachusetts — deep in one of America's largest Indian diaspora corridors — with the tournament arriving in Silicon Valley next.

articles.title: Martinelli in the 96th Minute. Brazil Break Japanese Hearts in Houston.
articles.excerpt: Casemiro's header and a last-gasp Martinelli strike complete a dramatic comeback as Carlo Ancelotti's five-time champions survive their biggest scare yet at the 2026 World Cup.
articles.image_caption: Gabriel Martinelli, whose stoppage-time goal sent Brazil into the World Cup Round of 16
articles.nri_angle: The World Cup knockout drama unfolded at NRG Stadium in Houston, home to one of America's largest Indian diaspora communities — the tournament in US cities is a once-in-a-generation experience for NRIs.

articles.title: 'We Need to Rethink': Muzumdar Demands Strategic Overhaul as India Women's T20 World Cup Failures Become a Pattern
articles.excerpt: Back-to-back group-stage exits, bowling frailties, and a captaincy question mark — coach Amol Muzumdar and experts map out what must change
articles.image_caption: Lord's Cricket Ground in London, where India's T20 World Cup campaign ended with a six-wicket loss to Australia
articles.nri_angle: The Indian diaspora in the UK invested emotionally and financially in tickets to watch the 2025 ODI World Cup champions play at Lord's, only to witness a repeat group-stage exit.
